text.text: Your clinic on one page. Start with Appointments for today, then Vaccines to call owners whose reminders are due, and use Pets and Owners for the people and animals behind every visit. Operational tracking only; medical records stay in your clinical system.
Reminders bring pets back for the preventive care that keeps them healthy and keeps the clinic busy. Done well, they feel like care, not marketing.
and filter for next due in the next 30 days with status Current.
. A pet set to Remembered never gets a reminder; a reminder for a pet who has died is one of the most painful mistakes a clinic can make.
Send the reminder in the owner's preferred way (text, email or phone call). Group all the pet's due vaccines into one message, and all the owner's pets into one message where you can.
"Hi Seraphina, Noodle is due for his lepto and kennel cough boosters next week. We have Thursday at 9:30 or Saturday at 11 with Dr. Joaquin. Reply with a time and we'll hold it."

Juniper's dental estimate was 890 dollars for a cleaning with two likely extractions. The owner signed the range and the anesthesia consent at drop-off; the vet called at 11:40 to say she was awake, and her recheck was booked for next week.
The front desk is not diagnosing. The job is to decide quickly whether a pet needs to be seen now, today, or can wait for a regular appointment, and to write down what the owner said.
Come in now or go to emergency
If the clinic cannot see them within minutes, give the address of the nearest emergency hospital.
Trouble breathing, blue or very pale gums
Collapse, seizures, or unable to stand
Swollen, hard belly with retching and nothing coming up (especially large dogs)
Known poisoning: chocolate, xylitol, antifreeze, rat bait, lilies for cats, human medication
Hit by a car or a fall, even if the pet seems fine
Male cat straining in the litter box and producing nothing
Heavy bleeding that does not stop with pressure
Vomiting or diarrhea more than three times, or with blood
Not eating for more than a day (cats) or two days (dogs)
Limping without putting weight on the leg
Can wait for the next appointment
A lump that has been there for weeks and is not changing
Mild itching or ear scratching without pain
Questions to ask on every sick call
What is the pet doing right now?
When did it start and is it getting worse?
Any chance they ate something they should not?
Write the answers on the appointment page so the vet reads them before walking in.
Mochi's owner called: vomiting four times since last night, still drinking. That is "seen today", so she was booked at 10:30 with Dr. Joaquin and told to come straight in if Mochi stopped drinking.
Never suggest a human medicine to give at home.

An emergency walks in: the front desk tells waiting owners plainly that a critical patient arrived and offers anyone who cannot wait a new time the same week.

A vet is out sick: call the day's routine visits first (wellness and vaccines move easily), keep sick visits and rechecks, and ask the remaining vet to take a longer list with a tech doing weights and histories.
The system or phones are down: keep a paper list of arrivals and calls, then enter it the same afternoon so reminders and estimates are not lost.
Stock check on vaccines and preventives; nothing close to expiry left at the back.

At close, the front desk notices Atlas's kennel cough booster is due on Wednesday and he is booked; Pickles is due for his senior wellness on Friday and is not confirmed, so he goes on the morning call list.

The front desk and reminder system of a small animal clinic: who is coming in today, which pets are due or overdue for vaccines, and the owners behind them. Medical records stay in your practice software; this is where the day is run.
: each visit with the pet, vet, reason, status and the estimate given to the owner.
: species, breed, sex and whether altered, weight, microchip and handling alerts the team should know before walking into the room.
: contact details and how each owner prefers to hear from you.
: every vaccine given, its term (six months, one year, three years), lot number and the next due date.
